subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name the blood vessels that enter and exit the kidney.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.49, VSAQ 67. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Text revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the memory tip no longer says artery in and vein out holds for every organ, because the liver receives most of its blood through the hepatic portal vein.

Excretory Products and their Elimination · 2 marks

steps.label: Vessel that enters
steps.why: The artery brings the blood that is to be filtered, so it must enter before any urine can be made.
common_mistakes: Naming the ureter. That carries urine, not blood.
steps.memory_tip: Artery in, vein out for the kidney.
steps.margin_note: One line each. Add the hilum for completeness.
lines: The blood vessel that enters the kidney is

steps.label: Vessel that leaves
steps.why: The vein carries away blood that has had its wastes removed, so it leaves by the same notch the artery entered.
common_mistakes: Naming the urethra. That is not a blood vessel.
Giving only one vessel when two are asked.
steps.memory_tip: Both use the same door, the hilum.
steps.margin_note: Name the hilum in the last line.
lines: The blood vessel that leaves the kidney is

lines.text: Both pass through the notch called the hilum

insider_note: Both vessels enter and leave at the hilum. Naming that notch is a safe extra line.
